2026-09-04T12:38:57.7750047Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7750440Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7750766Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7751783Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7752210Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7752727Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7754327Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7756083Z >
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7758399Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7760841Z >
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7761921Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7762693Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7762878Z ### How to Use
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7763121Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7763827Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7764551Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7764717Z ```bash
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7765287Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7766046Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7766662Z ```
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7766868Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7767133Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7767662Z ```bash
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7768202Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7768992Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7769885Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7770635Z ```
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7770838Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7771722Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7772613Z ```bash
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7773222Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7773913Z ```
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7774125Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7774464Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7775197Z ```bash
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7775737Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7778174Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7778975Z ```
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7779193Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7779475Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7779909Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7781558Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7783161Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7783336Z ```bash
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7783791Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7785284Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7786159Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7786481Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7787008Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7788024Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7788843Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7789313Z ```
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7789521Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7790275Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7791391Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7791572Z ```bash
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7792267Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7793160Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7793888Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7794334Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7794747Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7795553Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7796114Z ```
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7796319Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7796538Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7797366Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7798354Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7799351Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7800372Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7801772Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7802334Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7802510Z ### Notes
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7802736Z 
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7803355Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7804772Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7806035Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7807300Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7808511Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7809663Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7810654Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-04T12:38:57.7811568Z </mcp-clis>
